title: Forks on the dividing-crawler claim: dt/2 holds (gen 5); cutting actin production stops crawling and division; removing all food leaves 'undead' cells held up by rim actin
summary: Three tests on the world of 20261025T0828-c04-crawler-divide-claim (world.py here adds fork switches t_starve, t_cut, bV; defaults reproduce the claim). (1) dt/2 (dt 0.025, spf 100), seed 1: max generation 5, 15 persistent splits, merge/split 0.12, max 10.7 body lengths, against 4, 11, 0.20, 7.9 at dt=0.05 (dt_half/). (2) Rim layer does work: at t=300 actin production beta is cut to 0.2x (t_cut, seed 1). After the fork the mean body speed is 0.030 vs 0.136 in the uncut twin (90th percentile 0.05 vs 0.40), with 0 vs 2 later persistent splits and 12 vs 15 bodies at t=600 (rim_cut/post.txt, measured by tools/post.py from frames.npz); cells round up at once. The |P| rim passes the radial test in every seed of the claim (rim/core 2.1-3.1, rim/outside 5.5-6.2). (3) Negative for metabolism as built: removing all food at t=300 (t_starve, seeds 1 and 2) drives every body's content V to 0 by t~320, yet 12 and 13 small round bodies persist to t=600 (starve/). They are held up by actin pushing at the rim, because actin production has a floor (0.2 beta) independent of content. So the claim world does not show L4c metabolism: its cells do not die when starved. A fix (bV=1: actin production scaled by content density V/A) is being tested.

finding.operator: Ziebert-Aranson actin polarization rim with nutrient-modulated production
finding.control: branched fork at t=300 with the uncut twin (same seed); starvation fork on 2 seeds
finding.result: rim cut: speed 0.030 vs 0.136, later splits 0 vs 2; starvation: V->0 but 12/13 bodies persist (no deaths)
